items.title: The 10,000-hour rule
items.claim: Anders Ericsson's research on expertise was popularised as a '10,000-hour rule' by Malcolm Gladwell. What did Ericsson himself say about it?

options.text: He coined and endorsed the simple rule
He argued deliberate practice mattered, but rejected the simple hours-to-mastery shorthand
He said hours did not matter at all
He demonstrated 100 hours is sufficient for any sport

items.reveal_title: Ericsson pushed back on the round number
items.reveal:
Ericsson's Peak (2016) and earlier papers emphasised deliberate, structured practice with feedback, and noted that hours alone are insufficient. He criticised the 10,000-hour shorthand.

Macnamara et al. (2014) meta-analysis found practice accounted for variable proportions of expertise depending on domain.
items.why: Popular versions of research findings can outlive the researcher's own corrections.

items.title: Why the marathon is 26.2 miles
items.claim: The modern marathon distance of 26 miles 385 yards (42.195 km) was set in which year?
items.reveal_title: Set in 1908 to suit a royal viewing arrangement
items.reveal:
The London 1908 course was extended so the start at Windsor Castle and the finish at the royal box in White City stadium gave a distance of 26 miles 385 yards. The IAAF adopted it as standard in 1921.

Earlier modern marathons varied between about 25 and 26 miles.
items.why: Athletic standards often have administrative rather than scientific origins.

items.title: Title IX participation increase
items.claim: Title IX of the US Education Amendments (1972) banned sex discrimination in federally funded education, including athletics. By 2018, what proportion of US high school athletes were girls compared with 1971?

options.text: Roughly 10x more (about 295,000 in 1971 versus over 3 million by the 2010s)

items.reveal:
National Federation of State High School Associations data show girls' high school athletic participation rising from around 295,000 in 1971-72 to over 3.4 million in 2018-19.

Funding and facility disparities persist; the legal framework changed participation faster than parity.
items.why: Single policy interventions can reshape participation across decades.
